Private Transfer — Mercedes V Class 3–6 passengers, 1 carry-on + 1 checked bag each; water bottle included; drivers do not speak English (can add assistant/guide)

Flights — Expanded Module Detail

Arrivals

  • Most clients arrive via Madrid (MAD) or Barcelona (BCN) — both have direct flights worldwide
  • Málaga and Palma de Mallorca also used occasionally — direct flights from the US
  • ⚠️ Always include an M&G for first arrival — DMC's M&G Assistant meets at airport or hotel
  • All KT itineraries include a private transfer from airport to accommodation (even though MAD/BCN both have transit options to city center)
  • MAD → Madrid city center: 20–45 min drive (traffic-dependent)
  • BCN → Barcelona city center: 15–35 min drive (traffic-dependent) (compare to the earlier-noted Aerobús time of ~25 min and airport distance of 13km — consistent)

Domestic Flights — General Guidance

  • Can save time on short trips but can be pricey; not all city pairs have direct full-service routes
  • 💡 Rule of thumb: if a train route is more than 5 hours, suggest a flight transfer instead
  • Most common domestic routes involve Barcelona (east coast) — flight ~1 hr vs. train ~2.5 hrs, choice depends on client budget/preference

Common Domestic Flight Route Cheat Sheet

Route Recommendation
Barcelona – Seville Flight (~1.5 hrs) preferred
Barcelona – Granada Flight (~1.5 hrs) preferred, but limited carriers for direct flights
Barcelona – Bilbao Flight (~1.5 hrs) preferred
Barcelona – San Sebastián Train is 6 hrs; San Sebastián airport is small w/ limited flights — alternative: fly to Bilbao + ~1 hr private transfer to San Sebastián

Granada ↔ Barcelona — Special Case (exam-likely — booking logic/decision tree) - Train takes 6.5 hours — flying is much more time-efficient - ⚠️ Only airline offering a direct flight on this route is Vueling (budget) — KT Air will not book Vueling (doesn't meet KT service standards) - Options for this route: 1. DMCs book Vueling directly — must clearly set client expectations about budget-airline amenities 2. KT Air books a different routing with a layover in Madrid on a full-service airline (usually Iberia) 3. Client books their own flight 4. DMCs book the train — not recommended given the 6.5-hr length

Flights to Portugal & Morocco

  • No train service from Spain to Portugal or Morocco — clients fly, or take a private transfer
  • Common routes: flights Madrid → Lisbon or Albufeira; private transfers Seville → Lisbon or Albufeira

Booking Rates & DMC Capabilities

  • TMT has rate estimates for common domestic routes (assumes booking ≥2 months in advance — actual rates may vary)
  • Liberty Spain: can book domestic flights; cannot book Portugal/Morocco flights
  • Spaintop: can book both domestic AND Portugal/Morocco flights (Portugal/Morocco rates on request only)
  • KT Air: can book both domestic and Portugal/Morocco flights, but full-service airlines only
  • 💡 General tip: suggest business-class upgrades for a more comfortable flying experience

Trains — Expanded Module Detail

The Train Experience (illustrated via Madrid → Toledo → Barcelona)

  • Atocha Station (Madrid) — Madrid's largest train station, with routes throughout Spain & Europe
  • Shorter/commuter trains (e.g., Madrid → Toledo, ~30 min): one service level only (no first-class); no assigned seats — arrive early to sit together; luggage stowed in a stall at the front of each car, carry-ons in overhead storage; free Wi-Fi
  • High-speed/longer trains (e.g., Madrid → Barcelona, ~3 hrs): seat assignment printed on ticket; first-class and standard-class options; first-class = more legroom, sometimes free drinks/snacks; clients still stow their own luggage; free Wi-Fi
  • Arrival note: driver typically meets clients inside the train station, after the security checkpoint

When to Choose a Train

  • Spain's rail system is fast/reliable — factoring in airport transfer time, a train can beat flying
  • Trade-offs to weigh: some clients may be unfamiliar with navigating busy stations; clients must stow their own luggage (no porter service)

Fastest Train Journeys — High-Speed Route Times (exam-likely — memorize this grid) | From \ To | Madrid | Seville | Granada | Córdoba | Barcelona | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Madrid | — | 3h | 3h | 2h | 2h 30m | | Seville | 3h | — | 2h 30m | 1h | 5h 30m | | Granada | 3h | 2h 30m | — | 1h 30m | — | | Córdoba | 2h | 1h | 1h 30m | — | — | | Barcelona | 2h 30m | 5h 30m | — | — | — |

(— = no direct high-speed route / not a common pairing per this module)

  • 💡 Rule of thumb: trains departing from Madrid tend to be among the fastest routes to key locales
  • Comparison examples: Madrid–Barcelona train is ~3 hrs faster than driving; Seville–Granada train is roughly the same length as driving — always worth comparing train time vs. Google Maps driving time per specific route, since it varies

Tips for Booking Trains

  • Tickets are non-refundable
  • Seats cannot be confirmed in advance, but you can input the client's window/aisle preference

Private Transfers — Expanded Module Detail

Overview

  • Used for: transfers between locales, hotel-to-station/airport transfers, and getting clients to tours
  • All private transfers are built into TMT
  • ⚠️ Spain's driver fleet typically does not speak conversational English — drivers are not acting as tour guides, just ensuring on-time point A→B transport

Available Add-Ons

  • Assistant — helps with luggage
  • Local guide met en route — e.g., on a Seville → Granada transfer, clients can stop for a day tour in Córdoba, meeting a local guide there mid-journey (good upsell/itinerary-building idea)

Selecting the Right Car (exam-likely — capacity figures) | Vehicle | Passengers | Notes | |---|---|---| | Mercedes Class E | 2 | Standard sedan | | Mercedes Class S | 2 | More luxury sedan option — available in some locales as an upgrade from Class E | | Mercedes Class V | 3–6 | Van-style vehicle |

  • All car types hold 1 checked bag + 1 carry-on per person
  • ⚠️ In historic old towns (e.g., Barcelona's Gothic Quarter), drivers cannot drop off directly in front of the hotel — check hotel location carefully for clients with mobility issues

Spain Grand Tour — details - Tagline: A longer itinerary for those who want to immerse themselves in the culture/history of multiple regions — great for repeat travelers. More in-depth city exploration via full-day tours; visits the Andalusian "golden triangle" (Seville, Granada, Córdoba) plus Ronda, ending with leisure time in Costa del Sol. - Mix of private full-day & half-day tours, train travel, mid-level hotels; focus on history, culture, bucket-list highlights, authentic towns - Route logic: Barcelona → Madrid → Andalucía "golden triangle" (Seville, Granada, Córdoba) + Ronda → ends with leisure time in Costa del Sol - Córdoba: 2 nights; if no overnight time, can visit as a stop between Seville and Granada; ⚠️ busy during the Patios Festival (May) - Granada → Marbella: transfer - Marbella: beach/relaxation/golf; alternatives: Málaga (similar), Torremolinos/Fuengirola (known for beaches); add-ons: Gibraltar or Ronda/White Villages

✅ QUALIFYING QUESTIONS — MATCHING CLIENTS TO PRODUCT ✅

The guide has scattered tips throughout ("ask which artists they want to see," "check the hotel's definition of adult"). This page pulls the client-fit questions into one checklist, mapped to the itinerary/DMC/hotel decisions they actually drive. Use this as a pre-call prep sheet.

Ask the client... Why it matters Where the answer routes to
How many days/nights total? Determines which Job Aid itinerary template fits (5 days → Barcelona Discovery; 10 → Signature Spain; 14 → Grand Tour) Section “TOP ITINERARIES (Job Aid)”
First time in Spain, or repeat visitor? First-timers → hit the icons (Madrid + Andalusia + Barcelona); repeat visitors → go deeper/off-the-beaten-path (Valencia, Bilbao, wine regions) Section “TOP ITINERARIES (Job Aid)”, 1.17
What pace do they want — packed or leisurely? Drives half-day vs. full-day touring mix, and how many locales to include Section “TOP ITINERARIES (Job Aid)”, 1.13
Traveling with kids? What ages? Under ~12 often shares a room with 2 adults; determines Family Twist add-on and room configuration Section “DMCs IN SPAIN”, 1.14
Any mobility concerns? Rules out specific sites/hotels (Park Güell, Las Casas de la Judería properties, Medina Azahara) — see the new accessibility summary below Section “TOP SITES BY LOCALE (Job Aid)”, 1.14
Budget signal — Discovery, Premier, or Luxe? Determines hotel tier and whether to sequence Discovery→Premier if mixing Section “POPULAR HOTELS BY LOCALE (Job Aid)”
Cruise before or after? Affects which arrival/departure city makes sense and whether a pre/post-cruise city-only itinerary (Barcelona Discovery) fits better than a grand tour Section “TOP ITINERARIES (Job Aid)”, 1.17
Core interests — art, food, history, beaches, active? Routes to Golden Triangle depth (art), tapas/cooking classes (food), Andalusia (history), Marbella/Costa del Sol (beaches) Section “MADRID”–1.4, 1.15–1.18
What month are they traveling? Rules out/in Andalusia in summer heat, flags festival-driven hotel scarcity (Semana Santa, Feria de Abril, Patios Festival) Section “WEATHER BY LOCALE”, 1.5–1.17

♿ Accessibility & Mobility — Consolidated Summary

Mobility notes are scattered per-site throughout the guide; here they are in one place for a quick client-fit check.

Not mobility-friendly (steep terrain, stairs, uneven ground — flag before booking): - Park Güell, Casa Milà rooftop (Barcelona) - Medina Azahara (Córdoba) - Las Casas de la Judería properties in both Seville and Córdoba (narrow historic streets, multi-building layouts) - Albaicín walking tour (Granada) — steep roads

Mobility-friendly (ramps, elevators, designated entrances): - Prado Museum, Royal Palace (Madrid) - Reina Sofía, Thyssen-Bornemisza (Madrid) - Casa Batlló (Barcelona — has elevators, though rooftop access limited in peak season) - Most Hospes-brand hotels have at least 1 fully accessible room (verify specific room category — several have entry steps despite the accessible room itself being compliant)

💡 When in doubt, this is a "call the hotel/DMC to confirm" situation — general notes above are directional, not a guarantee.

🇵🇹 PORTUGAL

Portugal pairs naturally with Spain on multi-country itineraries — two of this guide's own live listings already sell it (Epic Iberian Journey, Spain & Portugal Signature), so it's worth knowing well even before a stand-alone Portugal itinerary comes up. General destination knowledge below (orientation, sites, culture, timing) is accurate and reference-ready. Anything Kensington-specific — preferred hotel lists, the actual Portugal DMC(s) and their tariffs, negotiated rates — is flagged ⚠️ and should be confirmed against the official Portugal Job Aid/TMT before it's used with a client, the same way Spain's own DMC and hotel data was sourced from KT's internal documents rather than general knowledge.

Portugal — Key Locales Overview

Portugal's tourism core sits in four areas most clients ask about, and that Kensington's own live itineraries already sell: Lisbon (the capital and default arrival point), Porto (the north, wine country's gateway), Sintra (a Lisbon day trip, occasionally an overnight), and the Algarve (the southern coast, Portugal's beach/resort region). The Douro Valley — Portugal's premier wine region — is usually sold as an extension from Porto or as part of a river-cruise product, not a stand-alone stop.

🏛️ LISBON

Why clients love it: Lisbon is one of Europe's oldest cities and one of its most photogenic — built across seven hills above the Tagus (Tejo) River, with pastel-tiled buildings, vintage yellow trams climbing impossibly steep streets, and golden late-afternoon light that's become a signature of the city's tourism marketing. It reads as more relaxed and less expensive than Madrid or Barcelona, while still delivering serious food, history, and nightlife — a common sell for clients who want "the next Spain" without repeating a trip they've already taken.

Getting there: Humberto Delgado Airport (Lisbon Airport, LIS) sits close to the city center, roughly a 15–20 minute transfer. Lisbon has direct flights from major US/Canada gateways and from Madrid and Barcelona (~1–1.5 hrs). There is no high-speed rail link to Spain — combined Spain-Portugal itineraries fly between the two countries or route via a river cruise.

Orientation — key neighborhoods:

NeighborhoodCharacter
AlfamaThe oldest district — a maze of narrow medieval streets below the São Jorge Castle; home to the Fado music tradition and some of the city's best viewpoints (miradouros)
BaixaThe flat, grid-planned downtown, rebuilt after the catastrophic 1755 earthquake; main shopping and the grand Praça do Comércio riverside square
Bairro Alto & ChiadoBairro Alto is Lisbon's nightlife district by night, quiet by day; Chiado (just below it) is upscale shopping, cafés, and theaters
BelémWest of the center, along the river — home to the Jerónimos Monastery, the Belém Tower, and the original Pastéis de Belém custard-tart bakery; usually a half-day outing rather than a touring base

Signature sites: The Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower (both UNESCO World Heritage Sites, both tied to Portugal's Age of Discoveries), São Jorge Castle (panoramic views over the Alfama and the river), and a ride on Tram 28, the historic yellow tram that winds through the oldest, steepest parts of the city — genuinely a sightseeing experience, not just transport, though it gets crowded and pickpocket risk is real on board.

Food & culture: Lisbon's food scene runs on fresh seafood (bacalhau — salt cod — appears in dozens of traditional preparations), pastéis de nata (custard tarts, best known from the original Belém bakery), and a strong café culture. Fado — Portugal's melancholic, guitar-accompanied musical tradition, recognized by UNESCO — is most authentically experienced in small Alfama tascas rather than large touristic dinner-show venues; worth differentiating for clients who want the real thing.

Best time to visit: Spring (Apr–Jun) and early autumn (Sep–Oct) — mild temperatures, manageable crowds. Summer (Jul–Aug) is hot, dry, and the busiest season, similar in feel to Madrid's summer. Winter is mild by northern-European standards but does bring more rain than most clients expect from a "sunny Portugal" mental image — worth setting that expectation.

Hotels: ⚠️ No Kensington-preferred property list confirmed yet for Lisbon in this guide — apply the same Discovery/Premier/Luxe framework used for Spain (see "Hotel Characteristics & Hotel Levels" in Training Job Aids) and confirm actual preferred properties via TMT/Job Aid before quoting. Baixa/Chiado and the riverside near Belém are generally the most walkable, well-located base areas.

🍷 PORTO

Why clients love it: Porto is Portugal's second city and the namesake of Port wine — a grittier, more intimate, and (many repeat visitors argue) more atmospheric alternative to Lisbon. The Ribeira district's stacked, colorful riverside houses along the Douro River are one of Portugal's most photographed views, and the historic Port wine lodges across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia make it a natural food-and-wine sell.

Getting there: Francisco Sá Carneiro Airport (Porto Airport, OPO), ~11 km from the city center, ~20–25 min by taxi/transfer; connected to downtown by metro as well. Direct flights from several European hubs and seasonal/limited North American routes; many US/Canada clients connect via Lisbon or a European gateway.

Signature sites: The Ribeira riverside district (UNESCO World Heritage), the Dom Luís I Bridge (a dramatic double-deck iron bridge with pedestrian access on both levels), Livraria Lello (an ornate early-20th-century bookstore often cited — with some myth-making — as a Harry Potter inspiration; expect a ticketed timed-entry system due to demand), and a Port wine lodge tour/tasting across the river in Vila Nova de Gaia.

Food & culture: Port wine is the obvious centerpiece — a fortified wine produced only in the Douro Valley and aged/blended in Porto's riverside lodges, with genuine differences between styles (Ruby, Tawny, Vintage) worth explaining to food-focused clients. The francesinha, a heavy, sauce-drenched sandwich, is Porto's most famous (and most polarizing) local specialty.

Best time to visit: Similar seasonal logic to Lisbon — spring and early autumn are the sweet spot. Porto is further north and slightly cooler/wetter than Lisbon year-round; pack for the possibility of rain even outside the official rainy season.

Hotels: ⚠️ No Kensington-preferred property list confirmed yet — apply the Discovery/Premier/Luxe framework and confirm actual picks via TMT/Job Aid. The Ribeira riverside and the upscale Foz do Douro (near the coast) are the two most commonly requested base areas.

🏰 SINTRA

Why clients love it: Sintra is a fairy-tale hill town roughly 30 minutes from Lisbon, packed with romantic 19th-century palaces and estates set into a lush, misty mountain landscape — genuinely one of the most visually striking day trips in Europe, and a near-mandatory add-on for any Lisbon-based itinerary. The whole historic center and its surrounding landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Getting there: Train from Lisbon's Rossio Station, ~40 minutes, or private transfer (~30–40 min by road). Almost always sold as a half-day or full-day trip from Lisbon rather than an overnight base, though an overnight can suit clients who want to see the palaces without the day-trip crowds (arrive first thing or stay late).

Signature sites: The Pena Palace (a flamboyantly colorful 19th-century Romanticist palace on a hilltop, Sintra's single most iconic image), the Quinta da Regaleira (an eccentric estate famous for its symbolic "Initiation Well," a spiral staircase descending underground), and the Moorish Castle ruins. ⚠️ Sites here involve real walking and stairs on uneven historic terrain — flag for clients with mobility concerns, similar to the Albaicín caution already noted for Granada.

Best time to visit: Go early — Sintra is notoriously overcrowded by mid-morning, especially in summer, since it's a single-lane-road town absorbing huge day-trip volumes from Lisbon. An early departure or a private guide who can sequence sites around tour-bus arrival times is a genuine value-add to mention to clients.

🍇 DOURO VALLEY

Why clients love it: The Douro Valley is Portugal's oldest demarcated wine region (one of the oldest in the world) and the exclusive source of true Port wine grapes — a landscape of steep terraced vineyards along the Douro River that's frequently compared to a "green Grand Canyon." It's Kensington's own Douro River Cruise itinerary's namesake region (see Section "Itineraries — Live Website Listings" under Spain, since that listing spans both countries).

Getting there: Usually visited as a day trip or overnight extension from Porto (~1–1.5 hrs by road), or as part of a multi-day river cruise along the Douro itself — not typically sold as a stand-alone destination without one of those two anchors.

Signature experiences: Vineyard and quinta (wine estate) visits with tastings, scenic river cruises through the terraced valley, and — for clients with more time — a stop in the historic town of Peso da Régua or Pinhão, the region's small rail/river hub.

Best time to visit: September–October (harvest season) is the most atmospheric and popular window, though it's also the most crowded and priciest; late spring is a quieter, still-beautiful alternative.

🏖️ ALGARVE

Why clients love it: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coastal resort region — dramatic ochre cliffs, sea caves, and beach towns that function as Portugal's answer to a Costa del Sol-style beach-and-relaxation stop, the same role Marbella plays at the end of a Spain Grand Tour–style itinerary.

Getting there: Faro Airport (FAO) serves the whole region, with direct flights from several European hubs and seasonal charter routes; less common for direct North American service, so many US/Canada clients connect via Lisbon.

Signature sites: The Benagil Sea Cave (a dramatic collapsed sea cave with a natural skylight, reachable by boat or kayak tour, and one of the most photographed spots in Portugal), and the town of Lagos, a historic base with easy access to the region's best beaches and cliff walks.

Best time to visit: Given this is a beach/relaxation stop, summer (Jun–Sep) is the desired season here, the same logic already used for Marbella in the Spain section — though spring/autumn are far less crowded and still comfortable for clients prioritizing golf or general leisure over beach time specifically.

Last Follow-Up (re-engagement / close-out)

For a client who has gone quiet after multiple touches. Three variations depending on how engaged they seemed:

Variation A — Standard check-in:

Subject: Are you still interested?

Hi [Client Name],
Since I haven't heard back from you, I wanted to check in and see whether you're still interested in planning your trip to [Destination], or should I pause your file? I might be able to discuss a package promotion if I know more details.

Variation B — Client was fairly involved already: skip the check-in question and send a promo itinerary directly instead.

Variation C — Softer pause-or-continue framing, with a current promo/rate offer:

Since I haven't heard back from you, I wanted to check in and see whether you'd like me to pause the case for now, or if you're still interested in discussing the details further for your trip to [Destination].

We're currently offering deals and limited contract rates for [Season/Year], and you can secure this rate only with a [X]% deposit, with the flexibility of making changes or cancellations up until [X] months prior to your trip and getting your deposit back (except for a $[X] pp admin fee).

Note: confirm current promo terms (deposit %, cutoff window, admin fee) with TMT before quoting — these change by season.

DORA — AI Research Assistant

Last updated: June 2026. DORA is Kensington's AI-powered research assistant — use it instead of manually searching Teams, SharePoint, Job Aids, or TMT. Access at dora.triparcservices.com → select "Login."

ModeUse When...
New ChatResearching a destination, DMC, or itinerary; finding curated restaurant recommendations; reviewing process guides or Kensington tools; accessing cruise selling resources; answering insurance/CFAR questions; drafting client correspondence in the Kensington voice
ProductSearching for hotels by destination, tier, or amenities; filtering by Premier status, room type, or facilities; accessing direct TMT links; viewing hotel locations on a map; finding tours/activities by destination or DMC

Tips for better results: Be specific about destination and travel style ("Luxury safari for a family of 4," not "Africa safari"). For hotel searches, include needs like "preferred," "accessible," "family-friendly," or "Luxe-level." For tours, include the experience type ("Walking food tour in Bologna," not "Italy tours"). Always open the tariff file to confirm exact pricing — DORA gives a summary and link, not the final number. Start a new chat when changing topics, since DORA carries context forward within a thread.

Feedback: Thumbs up = useful and accurate enough to act on. Thumbs down = inaccurate, incomplete, generic, or unhelpful — leave a short comment (e.g. "Hotel doesn't exist anymore," "Too generic, didn't help with this destination").

Vendors and Sourcing Rates

Kensington uses five vendor types to source and book hotel, tour, and transport rates. Each has a different rate type, booking process, and use case.

VendorRate TypeBooked ViaKey Note
DMCsStatic (KHP/TMT) or Dynamic (DMC Portal)TMT or DMC PortalAvailability check required before upload
Kensington Hotel Portal (KHP)Static competitive, ROR, Static DMC rates, TE Luxury, Ensemble Amenity/Preferred, Amadeus Leisure, non-preferred partner ratesTMT — TSR team books some rate types, DMCDynamic rates not available in KHP
Country & Regional PortalsDynamicPortal (external to TMT)Portal-specific SOPs apply
Kensington ContractedStatic competitive (KHP/TMT) or RORTMT — TSR team booksHotels vetted; SD can expedite peak requests
Dynamic HotelsDynamic (multiple external sources)TMTConfirm booking by emailing hotel after upload

Sourcing a missing hotel rate (pricing error, blocked dates, or missing data) — work through in order: (1) Check tariffs in Teams > Team Tours Sales Ops > Tariffs > Files. (2) Check the DMC portal if one exists. (3) Use Best Available Rate (BAR) from the hotel's own website — click through to the final booking screen to see all fees/taxes even if not booking. (4) Check Dynamic Hotels and KHP/TMT. (5) Ask in your country/regional Teams chat, only after exhausting other sources. (6) Reach out to the DMC directly if the trip is approaching booking. For Rates on Request (ROR), use the BAR as an estimated rate, then connect with the DMC for the exact contracted rate as the quote firms up. Missing tour rates follow the same steps minus hotel-specific sources, plus using a comparable rate from the same DMC as a placeholder. Missing transport rates add a public-fare search (trains/air) and a comparable-vehicle placeholder from a different supplier.

Tiered Hotels in TMT

The Tiered Hotel Program flags strong-value hotel options directly in TMT with a T1–T4 label beside the property name.

TierMeaning
T1 — FlagshipStrongest overall value
T2 — PreferredStrong options, very good value
T3 — Static/DynamicStatic direct-contracted and dynamic rate contract hotels
T4 — LegacyFormer Preferred Program

Tiers are based on discount below BAR, availability, promotions, amenities, and client experience — and are tied to Kensington-contracted hotels specifically, not DMC contracts. Prioritize T1 when it fits the client, strongly consider T2, and treat T3/T4 as informational rather than the primary focus. Best practice: always book the lowest available rate (LAR) — compare vendors against each other, compare a vendor against itself (static TMT rate vs. dynamic portal rate), and compare against direct contracts. When the direct hotel rate is lowest, book direct via TSR.

Working with Kensington Air

Last updated: Oct. 2025. KT Air Experts ensure flight itineraries align with the land experience and book only trusted, full-service airlines — quotes within 1 business day, responses within 4 hours, 24/7 support on bookings/changes/cancellations.

Submitting a request: On the case file page, click the three dots → "Air Quote Request." Submit only one request per case file with all flight needs included. Fill in arrival/destination airports, traveler count (children are up to age 12 for flights), dates and preferred time of day, and seat preference. Specify whether flights are included in the itinerary quote or billed separately. International = flights originating in the US/Canada crossing the Atlantic/Pacific, or to the Caribbean/Central/South America; Internal = everything else, including one-way flights to the US/Canada.

An Air Expert is assigned within ~3 business hours and responds within 1 business day, corresponding with the client or DE (DE is always copied). Submit a requote if trip details change, you have new details, the client requests a revision, or the Air team has already begun work. Once the client is ready to book, the AE gets DE approval on timing before booking and uploads the ticketed booking to TMT. Never promise refunds or discuss compensation on a cancellation — that's the AE's conversation with the client.

Flight TypeFee
Domestic, not included in tour cost$50/person (economy)
International$150/person (economy) · $300/person (business)
Group bookings$250 flat fee

Adding flights after an itinerary's flights are already booked triggers the fee for the new flight type (e.g. adding international after domestic was already booked = international fee applies). A client's own request for an air quote via the website contact form is an "RAQ," routed to the RAQ Air Support Team — they won't reach out until the DE has connected with the client first.

Travel Insurance for Canadians

Last updated: July 2025. Kensington's referral partner for Canadian-resident clients is Manulife. To refer a client, email travel_referral@manulife.ca with the client copied, using a template covering: client name, email/phone, tour confirmation date, travel dates, non-refundable amount per person, Kensington Tours code (TTNKENT), agent ID, and agent contact info.

Cancel For Any Reason (CFAR): the All-Inclusive Policy must be purchased within 72 hours of confirming the tour to qualify. It allows cancellation up to 14 days before the coverage start date with a 50% refund via insurance claim, no questions asked.

Hotel Styles Cheat Sheet

A shared vocabulary for classifying hotels — useful when describing any property in this guide, Spain or otherwise.

StyleCharacteristicsExamples
HistoricHistoric building converted to a hotel; may carry local heritage-listing restrictions on renovation; each room often unique; bathroom configs vary; AC/heating sometimes limited; strong sense of place, may need updatingThe Abbey Hotel (Bath), Château Belmont (Tours)
American ChainBrand-affiliated with strict amenity/design guidelines; standardized globally; may lack character, especially at Discovery/Premier tiersJW Marriott Marquis Dubai, Hilton City Munich
ContemporaryModern, design-forward, sometimes minimalist or avant-garde; avoid unusual/controversial décor or adult-only artShinta Mani Angkor (Siem Reap)
ArtOwned by an art collector, public areas run as gallery space; taste-driven, may or may not connect to the destination; same controversial-art caution appliesHotel Le Negresco (Nice)
Tented Camps & LodgesSelf-contained, immersive, usually full-board; nature/outdoor-activity focus; individual units with ensuite bath, central communal dining; some unfenced African camps require staff escort after darkDenali Backcountry Lodge (Alaska), Saseka Tented Lodge (Kruger)
ResortsLarge footprint, extensive on-site grounds/amenities (restaurants, spa, pools, kids' clubs); food plans range breakfast-only to all-inclusive; golf resorts include in-house championship-affiliated coursesFour Seasons Resort Alexandria, The Fairmont St Andrews

Hotel Characteristics & Hotel Levels

Why hotels matter: hotels are one of the biggest factors in client satisfaction and can make or break the trip. Selection criteria: Location (sense of place, safety, fit with itinerary flow), Size (match to client preference — intimate boutique vs. full-service), Style (fit the client's taste and goals), Dining (on-site options, dress code, reservation requirements). Be proactive discussing room size/bedding, AC, views, and accessibility — and always clarify what's included in the rate (breakfast, club access, half board, full board). Kensington hotels should always include breakfast.

LevelBest For
DiscoveryComfortable, clean, well-located; value/convenience/essential amenities; clients who spend most of their time exploring rather than at the hotel
PremierOften the best overall fit — balance of comfort, character, location, amenities; higher-quality experience without ultra-luxury expectations
LuxeExceptional service, luxury accommodations, premium dining, exclusive experiences; clients seeking pampering, privacy, top-tier amenities

Qualify before recommending: ask how important the hotel is to the trip overall and what "luxury" means to this specific client — prior hotel experiences are a good proxy. Set expectations: keep hotel quality consistent through the itinerary, end on the strongest hotel when possible, and don't rely on star ratings alone. Key takeaway: match the hotel to the client, not the rating.

TMT — Building a Custom Service

Last updated: Jan. 2026. Prioritize personalizing an existing TMT service over building a custom one. Only build custom when: the service isn't available in TMT, it's a specialized touring request, a hotel isn't available in hotel tools, or you need a variation of an existing tour.

From scratch: in your quote (Create Quote/Requote), click the orange "C" button on the relevant day/slot, then the yellow circle-arrows (🔄) to edit. Converting an existing service: add the existing TMT service via the "➕" icon, click the orange "C" next to it to convert, then edit via the yellow circle-arrows (🔄). Always confirm with the vendor that the change is possible and get the correct rate before finalizing — this isn't optional.

Formatting standards (so custom services look consistent with built ones on the client's quote):

Service TypeFormatExample
TourTour Name (Length) – Service ProviderPrague Food and Culture Walking Tour (4 hrs) – Guide
TransferTransfer Type – Service ProviderTrain Station Transfer – Vehicle/Driver
Activity/DiningService Name – InclusionDining Reservation at Dill – Meal Paid Locally
TransportDeparture – Arrival [Length] – Provider (Inclusion)Rome – Naples [1 hr 10 min] – First Class Train Tickets
HotelHotel Name (Meals) (Room Category)Hôtel de Nell (B) (Junior Suite)

Use standard provider labels: Guide; Vehicle/Driver; Vehicle/Driver/Guide (2 people); Vehicle/Driver-Guide (1 person); First/Standard Class Train Tickets; Entrance Fees Included/Not Included; First Class Air (Separate Purchase). Select the service type in the Service and Category dropdowns so it formats correctly on the client's quote, and always set Source/Destination and assign the vendor with a rate.

Descriptions should set clear expectations, paint a picture with "wow moment" language, and specify inclusions/exclusions if it's a variation of another tour. Hotel room descriptions can be copied from the hotel's own website — include room size and max capacity for family rooms. Photos: use an Official Image via Cloudinary, or a public-domain/royalty-free web image — the most recognizable highlight of the tour/locale, and for hotels the scope of the room, not just the bed. Always preview in client view before sending.

🎓 Certification Exam — Confirmed Traps & Notes (Passed Attempt, 78.9%)

Compiled from a real passed certification attempt (practice quiz + full 30-question final exam). This is different from the rest of this guide's content: everything below reflects what the actual KT answer key rewarded or penalized on a real exam, including a few points where the answer key disagreed with general destination logic. Where something is still unconfirmed, that's stated explicitly — treat those as open questions, not settled facts.

Wine Regions

Q: Clients visiting Lisbon/Madrid/Barcelona want a La Rioja stop but there's no time to add another locale — what 2 alternate wine regions?

  • ✅ Ribera del Duero — ~2 hrs from Madrid, Tempranillo-driven reds, same style profile as Rioja
  • ✅ Penedès — ~45 min–1 hr from Barcelona, known for cava, increasingly still wines too
  • ❌ Jerez (near Cádiz) and Rías Baixas (Galicia) are both excellent but far from Madrid/Barcelona — recommending them adds a genuinely new locale, defeating the purpose of the question.

💡 The logic pattern: the correct answer is always the wine region(s) that are day-trip-able from cities already on the itinerary — not just "any good wine region in Spain."

Madrid

General public sources (the official Mezquita site) show it's open daily with only reduced hours on Dec 24/25/31 and Jan 1 — closely matching the question's wording — but KT's answer key disagreed. Double-check this specific question against the KT certification document directly before a next attempt.

Hotel Tiering — ⚠️ the biggest trap on the exam

Premier-level clients ≠ Luxe-tier hotels. This distinction cost real points on the exam. A Luxe-tier hotel is a mismatch for a client explicitly described as "Premier-level" — don't default to the most famous/grandest name in a city just because it's the best-known property.

Corrected Premier-tier picks for a connecting-rooms/suites, city-center, Madrid + Barcelona + Seville client:

  • Madrid: H10 Villa de la Reina (not Hotel Orfila — reads as a small Luxe boutique)
  • Barcelona: Hotel Catalonia Catedral (not Olivia Plaza)
  • Seville: H10 Casa de la Plata (not Alfonso XIII — Luxe tier, too far above Premier)

(The original exam attempt scored partial credit, 2.22/3.33, having selected Alfonso XIII + H10 Villa de la Reina + Hotel Catalonia Catedral — Alfonso XIII was almost certainly the wrong pick given the tiering trap.)

💡 KT Size Categories — separate from the Discovery/Premier/Luxe tier system, this is about room count, and was confirmed correct on the exam:

  • Villa Oniria → Boutique (25–100 rooms)
  • Alfonso XIII → Medium (100–250 rooms)
  • Neri Hotel → Small (<25 rooms)

⚠️ Still unconfirmed (general-market guesses only, not exam-verified) — this guide's own Hotels by Tier reference above already flags two of these three as worth double-checking against the actual KT tier document, for the same reason:

  • Hospes Palacio del Bailío → guessed Luxe
  • Hospes Casas del Rey de Baeza → guessed Premier
  • Olivia Plaza → guessed Discovery

Cathedral Etiquette & Dietary Accommodations

  • Must cover shoulders and knees when visiting cathedrals in Spain — standard modest dress code enforced at religious sites regardless of season/weather.
  • Traditional tapas tours run fixed stops with set, often meat/seafood-heavy menus — vegan accommodation is not guaranteed on this tour type.

Itinerary Quality-Check Patterns ("what's wrong with this quote" questions)

These questions test spotting errors in sample itineraries. Recurring error types to scan for:

  1. Missing arrival transfers — e.g., a private transfer TO a train station is shown, but no transfer FROM the destination train station to the hotel on arrival.
  2. Hotel tier/room category inconsistency across days — e.g., a "Grand Deluxe Room" at a top luxury hotel one day, then a "Standard Room" at a mid-tier hotel the next, with no explanation.
  3. Leisure days with no built-in activity — a "day at leisure" should still include a suggested tour/activity; if a Shore Excursion or similar was swapped in instead of a "tour," that's flagged as an inconsistency too.
  4. Repeated site visits — two different tours on different days visiting the exact same site (redundant/wasted time).
  5. Do NOT flag: guide-only tours (no vehicle/driver) when the tour is a walking tour — that's correct, not an omission. Don't assume every day needs its own city tour if sightseeing is already covered on an adjacent day.

⚠️ Only partial credit (1.66/3.33) was scored on both itinerary-error questions on the exam — treat this list as directionally useful but not fully verified.

Description updated to match the built itinerary

Phone: build rapport (confident intro, warm demeanor, use the client's name, react with emotion); ask qualifying questions and rephrase for clarity; listen actively and refer back to notes; share expertise by connecting Kensington's value to the client's specific motivations. Email: customized subject line; sell yourself/Kensington/the destination; mention private guided and personalized itineraries; clear and concise, bullet points for highlights, formal address and tone. Always record all communication — lead scenario and call notes — in TMT.

Sending a quote: Save & Send Quote → review itinerary name/description → Next → review images → Next → review optional activities → Save & Send Quote again → confirm meals → Ok. On the yellow bar, choose the correct email template (e.g. "01 – First Engagement Attempt Email"), click Create Email, add the correct recipients, customize the email, and confirm both the hyperlink and the copy/paste URL are present before sending.
